title: Biology Eats the Market — Max vs Lena (Special)
description:
A one-off special. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) debate Antonio Linares's "bio/acc basket": his claim that biology drives most market returns over the next decade, and his four picks. Nautilus (NAUT) reads the proteome, Recursion (RXRX) designs drugs with A.I., ImmunityBio (IBRX) reboots the immune system with Anktiva, and MiNK Therapeutics (INKT) takes iNKT cell therapy after solid tumors. Max makes the case from the post and its 33-minute video: biology becomes code, a read, design, reboot and strike stack, disciplined management teams, and pharma money already flowing into Recursion. Lena pushes back with the latest filings: Nautilus's first revenue of about $0.2M and its Broadscale delay, Recursion's cash burn, ImmunityBio's 45x sales valuation and the FDA warning letter, and MiNK's roughly $9M cash plus a 17-patient phase 2 with zero responses. A made-up guest, Nigel, drops by to heckle the whole idea of "platform" biotech.

Source (credit): Antonio Linares (@alc2022) on X, Sep 28, 2026, https://x.com/alc2022/status/2104620231922745534 (post and attached video).
Also referenced: Q2 2026 results and filings from Nautilus, Recursion, ImmunityBio and MiNK; ImmunityBio's FDA warning letter and PDUFA date; MiNK's AACR 2026 phase 2 poster; market prices as of the Sep 28, 2026 close. Numbers are rounded. The hosts flag claims they couldn't verify on air. Nigel is fictional. This is not investment advice.

Chapters: 1. Biology is the new compute; 2. Read it, then design it; 3. Reboot and strike; 4. A stack or four lottery tickets?.

title: Anthropic Files Its S-1 — $16B Revenue, an $81B Paper Loss & a One-Share Founder Vote
description:
Special edition: Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on Oct 26, 2026 (Nasdaq: ANT; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley lead). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go through the filing: $16.3B H1 revenue (+1,304%), the $80.7B GAAP loss (mostly convertible-note revaluation), Q2 operating profit, $265.6B in purchase commitments and $321.4B in leases, the SpaceX, Microsoft, Amazon and Google deals, the LTBT, Founder LLC (50.1% vote) governance, market reaction, OpenAI, and read-across to the AI Infrastructure, AI Verticals and Musk theses. There is no price range or share count yet. Valuation ($1.5–2T) and timing (~Nov 19–20) come from press reports, not the filing. Graham and Wanjiru are fictional call-in characters.
Sources: SEC EDGAR S-1, Anthropic, CNBC live, Reuters/Investing.com, CoinDesk, Yahoo Finance, Stock Titan.

title: All-In This Week: Anthropic's IPO Wobble and the Open-Source Flood — Max vs Lena
description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Sep 21–29, 2026. Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic through all six episodes released that week: the main show, episode 290 ("Anthropic IPO at Risk, Meta's Muse Pop, Token Prices Fall, Open Source Gains Share, Alignment Fails", Sep 25), plus the Summit and interview episodes with Naveen Rao (Sep 21), Blake Scholl (Sep 22), Steve Hilton & Spencer Pratt (Sep 22), Luca Ferrari (Sep 23) and Daniel Ek (Sep 28).

Topics: "labs" vs. companies and product liability; the flood of open-weight models and the claimed flip in token share; whether Anthropic's IPO is in trouble (Polymarket odds, super-voting shares, Chamath's "$1 trillion or less" math, Sacks' "stable duopoly on a hamster wheel"); Bernie Sanders' superintelligence bill, Trump, Bessent and Obama; Meta's Muse, agents and the App Store's 30% cut; alignment, Claude's constitution and Anthropic's wet lab; AI's energy wall (Naveen Rao's dynamical computer, Boom's jet engines for data centers); Bending Spoons' buy-and-fix model; California's governor race; and Daniel Ek's $499 Neko Health scan.

Made-up guest: Dev, a fictional quant, joins briefly in the Anthropic chapter. He is invented for this episode and speaks for no real fund.

Sources: the official All-In episode descriptions and timestamps (RSS feed and YouTube), published episode transcripts (Happy Scribe) for five episodes, and our own Whisper transcription of the Daniel Ek episode's audio, cross-checked against published summaries. Hosts only describe what the besties said, and they don't imitate their voices. Where a transcript didn't make clear who said something, we say "one of them". Numbers are rounded and are the speakers' claims (for example valuations, Polymarket odds, token-share charts and company stats) unless we say otherwise. This is not affiliated with All-In and is not investment advice.

Chapters: 1. This week on All-In; 2. They're not labs, they're companies; 3. The open-source flood; 4. Is Anthropic's IPO in trouble?; 5. Bernie, Trump, Obama and the politics of AI; 6. Muse, agents and the App Store's thirty percent; 7. Alignment, Claude's constitution and the wet lab; 8. The energy wall: Naveen Rao and Boom's jet engines; 9. Bending Spoons: buying product-market fit; 10. California: Steve Hilton and Spencer Pratt; 11. Daniel Ek, Neko and the body scan; 12. What we'd watch next.

title: All-In This Week: Is Claude Conscious? — Max vs Lena
description:
An unofficial recap of the past week of the All-In podcast (Chamath Palihapitiya, Jason Calacanis, David Sacks and David Friedberg), Oct 3–10, 2026. Only one All-In episode was released since last week's recap: the main show, episode 292, "Is Claude Conscious? Pope Rejects, Model Welfare Movement, OpenAI's Math Backlash, France Riots" (released Oct 9, 10:06 PM ET). Max (bull) and Lena (skeptic) go topic by topic.

Topics: the New York Times report on Anthropic hosting religious leaders on Claude's possible consciousness and the Vatican episode; Friedberg's "birth of a new religion" view and Chamath's Descartes steelman; Sacks on the Claude Constitution's "conscientious objector" language and a played Mustafa Suleyman clip (the "epistemic hall of mirrors"); market vs. externalities, Chamath's three goals of alignment, and Roko's Basilisk; OpenAI's 700+ math papers, the "loops" idea, verifiability, and Chamath's pushback; the missing cryptography results (speculation) and expert gatekeeping; France's strikes and riots, Friedberg's "socialism point of guaranteed return", Sacks on subsidies; bond vigilantes, debt-to-GDP and yields; headless agents (Grok Bot, Dots), and Chamath's "software IP is worthless" claim.

Made-up call-ins: Callum, a fictional Dublin philosophy-of-mind researcher, and Graham, a fictional Manchester bond strategist. Both are invented for this episode and speak for no real person or firm.
